class: On a target copy without VCS metadata, the candidate's own new test file fails (six setup errors, one call failure, all from git exiting 128); these are candidate-owned and route to a builder repair, not to a runner-fault hold.

inputs.note: Synthetic: the log does not carry the diff or the environment declaration; these are the facts of the incident (the file was new in the candidate; the target is a copy without .git).

variants.change: inputs.changed_files = [] (the same errors in a file the candidate did not touch)
one of the ERRORs is a collection error of the same file instead of a setup error
the summary line reports 7 errors while 6 ERROR entries are listed (unaccounted count)

notes: One gate run, one result (found); the two expected entries are the per-item ownership classifications of that result, in log order of kind: the six setup ERRORs, then the one FAILED. All pass note 07's rule: a test node in a file the candidate added, setup section, traceback through that file, not an import error, count fully accounted. The FAILED test has the same cause (git cat-file in the call phase); it is candidate-owned as an ordinary failure. Both go to the builder with the environment facts; runtime verification on the package artifact should surface this before merge (note 13). Variants are runner/environment faults (a hold); runner_fault is proposed.
